data.one_liner: ActionCable client port in dart for web, dartVM and flutter
data.what_it_does: Connects to Rails ActionCable websocket servers, handles subscriptions, and allows performing actions on channels. It supports web, dartVM, and Flutter platforms.
use_when: You need to connect a Flutter or Dart app to a Ruby on Rails ActionCable backend
You require real-time websocket communication using the ActionCable protocol
avoid_when: You are using a standard REST API without WebSockets
Your backend uses a custom WebSocket protocol instead of Rails ActionCable
strengths: Native Dart port of the ActionCable protocol
Easy connection and channel subscription methods
weaknesses: Minimal configuration documentation beyond basic usage
data.setup_notes: Add web_socket_channel dependency and use ActionCable.connect with your websocket URL.

alternatives.name: web_socket_channel
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want raw WebSocket communication without being tied to the Rails ActionCable protocol.

alternatives.name: dio
alternatives.why_pick_it: If your backend primarily uses HTTP REST requests rather than real-time WebSockets.
